newsitem.title: USA: Thousands attend Shabazz funeral in New York.
newsitem.headline: Thousands attend Shabazz funeral in New York.

text.p: Thousands of people attended an Islamic funeral service on Friday for Betty Shabazz, widow of slain U.S. civil rights leader Malcolm X, who died from burns she suffered in a fire allegedly set by her grandson.
Mourners crowded into the Islamic Cultural Centre in Manhattan for the private service four days after Shabazz succumbed to burns over 80 percent of her body. She was 63.
Among the notables were former boxing champion Muhammad Ali, New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and Wallace Muhammad, the son of Elijah Muhammad, founder of the Nation of Islam black Moslem group.
All six of Shabazz's daughters attended the service, including Qubilah Shabazz, whose 12-year-old son Malcolm is accused of setting the fatal fire.
Shabazz's body lay in a bronze casket, facing east toward Mecca. Hundreds of floral arrangements were delivered for the service.
"She can stand as an example of a person who met her adversity and transcended it," said former mayor David Dinkins as he entered the building.

Shabazz, an activist for black women and a champion of human rights, was badly burned in the June 1 blaze at her apartment in Yonkers, New York. Doctors performed five skin-graft operations before she died.

New York City's medical examiner has ruled that her death was a homicide. Malcolm Shabazz, who allegedly set the fire with gasoline, has been charged with juvenile delinquency and the Shabazz family attorney said he expected additional charges would be filed.
Shabazz was to be buried next to her husband's grave at Ferncliff Cemetery in suburban Hartsdale, New York. He was gunned down at Harlem's Audubon Ballroom on Feb. 21, 1965.
A trained nurse, she earned a doctorate in education and at the time of her death was a public relations administrator at Medgar Evers College in Brooklyn, New York.
Thousands of people filed past her closed casket to pay respects during a two-day public wake. It was held at the same Harlem funeral home as her husband's wake 32 years ago.
